samples.summary: Session mirror pins the preference for the rest of the session, so later cross-tab changes are ignored until a write succeeds in this tab
samples.evidence: `if (memoryFormat !== null) return memoryFormat;` — `memoryFormat` is only cleared on a successful `localStorage.setItem` in this tab (line 66). Once one write fails (quota / SecurityError), `subscribe` still fires `onChange` on the `storage` event from another tab, but `getDateFormat` keeps returning the stale mirror, so the UI never reflects the other tab's change and never recovers even if storage becomes writable again. Clearing the mirror in the `storage` handler (or when a read yields a valid differing value) would allow recovery.

samples.summary: `formatListDate`'s injectable `now` is silently ignored in the `relative` branch, so the two formats disagree about the clock
samples.evidence: `return format === "exact" ? formatExactDate(value, now) : formatRelativeTime(value);` — `formatRelativeTime` takes no `now` and always uses the wall clock. A caller (or test) passing a fixed `now` gets a deterministic result for "exact" and a wall-clock-dependent one for "relative"; the injected clock is accepted then dropped, a silent contract violation rather than a compile error.

samples.summary: Guarded read still does not validate the stored theme value, so junk in storage is applied as a CSS class
samples.evidence: `return (readStoredTheme(storageKey) as Theme) || defaultTheme;` — `readStoredTheme` returns `string | null` and the cast asserts without checking that it is "dark" | "light" | "system". A tampered/legacy value such as "blue" flows into the effect at line 87 (`root.classList.add(theme)`), adding a bogus class and leaving the app in neither theme. The same change added an `isFormat` validator for the date preference (date-format-preference.ts:26), so the omission here is inconsistent. Pre-existing line, but it is the line this change wraps.

samples.summary: Every date cell allocates its own external-store subscription and two `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instances per render
samples.evidence: `DateCell` calls `useDateFormat()` (one window listener pair per cell, i.e. 2 per row) and both `formatFullDateTime` and `formatListDate` construct a fresh `Intl.DateTimeFormat` on each render. Correctness is unaffected — the snapshot is a stable primitive — but hoisting the preference read to the table and memoizing formatters would avoid O(rows) listeners/allocations per re-render.

finding.summary: Memory fallback is unreachable when writes fail but reads succeed (e.g. QuotaExceededError), so the preference silently reverts
finding.evidence: `getDateFormat` returns the stored value first (line 41-42) and only consults `memoryFormat` if the read threw or the stored value is absent/junk. The failure mode the new code claims to handle is not only all-or-nothing SecurityError: `localStorage.setItem` also throws QuotaExceededError (full storage / iOS Safari) while `getItem` keeps working. In that case storage still holds the previous valid value (say "relative"), `setDateFormat("exact")` sets `memoryFormat = "exact"`, the write throws and is swallowed, the CHANGE_EVENT fires, subscribers re-read via `getDateFormat`, the read succeeds and returns "relative" — the Settings `Select` snaps back to the old value with no explanation, exactly the outcome the comment on lines 61-64 says the try/catch prevents. A correct fix is to consult `memoryFormat` first (or set it only when the write actually fails and prefer it over the stale stored value). Note the new test masks this: it mocks BOTH `setItem` and `getItem` to throw, so the read-works/write-fails combination is never exercised.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim — that `getDateFormat` "returns the stored value first (line 41-42) and only consults `memoryFormat` if the read threw" — is not true of this repository. In packages/frontend/src/lib/date-format-preference.ts, line 48 is `if (memoryFormat !== null) return memoryFormat;`, which executes BEFORE the `localStorage.getItem` call on line 50. The mirror is therefore preferred over a stale stored value, which is exactly the fix the finding prescribes. `setDateFormat` sets `memoryFormat` only in the catch branch (line 72) and clears it on a successful write (line 66), which is the second prescribed half ("set it only when the write actually fails"), and also prevents a stale mirror from outvoting a key another tab cleared. Consequently the described failure chain (write throws QuotaExceededError, subscribers re-read, read succeeds and returns the previous "relative", Select snaps back) cannot occur — line 48 short-circuits and returns "exact". The secondary claim that the tests mask the case is also wrong: tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts:82-99 mocks ONLY `setItem` to throw QuotaExceededError, asserts storage still holds "relative" (line 94) and that `getDateFormat()` returns "exact" (line 95), i.e. the read-works/write-fails combination is directly exercised; :101-114 covers the inverse stale-mirror invariant. Grep confirms this is the only implementation of getDateFormat/memoryFormat, with a single consumer in src/app/settings/page.tsx, so there is no other copy exhibiting the described ordering.
